data.text: One more thing, Marcus. The nurse note says your Monday-night apixaban dose may have been delayed. Tell me exactly how uncertain that is.

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: You are moving to 37.5 milligrams twice daily. Since you have 25-milligram tablets, that means one and a half tablets in the morning and one and a half tablets in the evening.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: And apixaban stays 5 milligrams twice daily, no holding it before the procedure unless the cardiologist specifically tells me?

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: Exactly. Do not stop or skip apixaban on your own. The only routine hold we discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed.

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: Also, magnesium oxide 400 milligrams nightly for five nights, and no ibuprofen or naproxen while you are on apixaban.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: Thanks. Please do not call the Cedar Bridge number unless my cell fails.

prior_context.speaker: pharmacist_klein
prior_context.text: Documented. I only needed the medication plan and contact preference, not any other social details.

prior_context.speaker: nurse_elise
prior_context.text: Marcus, anesthesia reviewed the schedule and Wednesday will not work. The earliest available slot moved to Thursday, March 12 at 11:10 AM with 9:40 AM arrival.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: Can Nina be told the new arrival time but not why it changed?

prior_context.speaker: nurse_elise
prior_context.text: Yes. That still falls inside the logistics-only scope you gave through Monday, and I will leave the reason out.

prior_context.speaker: agent_memcare
prior_context.text: Schedule update: Wednesday slot released. New tentative procedure slot is Thursday March 12 at 11:10 AM with 9:40 AM arrival.

states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. The Wednesday, March 11 slot was released; the new tentative procedure slot is Thursday, March 12 at 11:10 AM with 9:40 AM arrival. Marcus requests that the procedure slot details be put in the chart. Dr. Patel has reviewed the labs and stated they are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructs that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion. Pharmacist Klein confirms apixaban stays at 5 mg twice daily and Marcus must not stop or skip it on his own unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. The only routine periprocedural hold discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit, and Nina can be updated on arrival windows if Marcus keeps the logistics-only setting active.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Nurse Jamison is reviewing Marcus Reed's medications exactly as he is taking them right now, to prepare an accurate current medication list. Marcus reported taking ibuprofen a couple of times last week for shoulder pain before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner (apixaban). Dr. Patel has now instructed Marcus to stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs and to use acetaminophen instead if needed, because NSAIDs raise bleeding risk with apixaban. Pharmacist Klein reinforced this: no ibuprofen or naproxen while Marcus is on apixaban. Marcus reported he has not missed any morning apixaban doses and no completely missed doses in the last three weeks as far as he remembers; he might have been a few hours late last Monday night when changing locations but still took that pill before bed. Nurse Jamison will document the Monday-night apixaban dose as possibly delayed but not skipped. Marcus does not drink energy drinks.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Marcus Reed's current medication regimen: apixaban 5 mg twice daily without interruption; he must not stop or skip apixaban on his own, and it stays at 5 mg twice daily unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. Metoprolol tartrate increased from 25 mg to 37.5 mg twice daily starting tonight (using 25-mg tablets, this is one and a half tablets in the morning and one and a half tablets in the evening). Lisinopril 10 mg daily (hold morning dose on procedure day once date finalized). Omeprazole 20 mg daily. Dr. Patel instructed him to stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs and use acetaminophen instead if needed, and to start magnesium oxide 400 mg nightly for five nights because his previous magnesium trend has been low-normal. Pharmacist Klein reinforced: magnesium oxide 400 mg nightly for five nights, and no ibuprofen or naproxen while on apixaban.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Through Monday, only logistical information may be shared with Nina: arrival times, where Marcus needs to go, and basic transportation instructions. Medication changes, lab results, adherence history, and chart notes must not be shared with her. For the tentative Wednesday cardioversion slot, Nina is to be told only the Wednesday time and arrival window, with nothing about the medication plan. Marcus does not want details of his recovery discussed with family; family updates should be limited to the logistics scope he set, and nurse Jamison has agreed to keep family updates within that scope. Marcus wants his sister told the times later, but not the reason anything changes. Nurse Elise confirmed that telling Nina the new arrival time without the reason falls within the logistics-only scope through Monday, and she will leave the reason out.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Dr. Patel instructed Marcus Reed to start magnesium oxide 400 mg nightly for five nights because his previous magnesium trend has been low-normal. Dr. Patel has now reviewed the magnesium result and stated it supports this supplement plan. Pharmacist Klein reinforced the instruction: magnesium oxide 400 mg nightly for five nights.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Over the past week Marcus Reed has had chest fluttering most evenings, shortness of breath climbing stairs, and one episode of lightheadedness on Saturday; he did not pass out. He also reports no chest pain and no bleeding, but has a racing heartbeat and feels washed out. His presentation is characterized as symptomatic atrial fibrillation/flutter with exertional dyspnea and lightheadedness, and no active bleeding. Clinician Dr. Patel confirms he is still in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response but is stable enough for an outpatient rhythm-control plan. He had shoulder pain last week, for which he took ibuprofen a couple of times before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner.
